edges.subject: GRN
edges.quote: heterozygous mutations in the GRN gene, resulting in haploinsufficiency, were found to be one of the main causes of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD).

edges.subject: frontotemporal lobar degeneration
edges.quote: FTLD is a clinically heterogenous disease that results in the progressive atrophy of the frontal and temporal lobes of the brain.

edges.subject: GRN
edges.quote: homozygous GRN mutation leads to neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis, a lysosomal storage disease.

edges.subject: PGRN
edges.quote: several links between PGRN and the lysosome have been established, including the existence of two independent lysosomal trafficking pathways.

edges.subject: PGRN
edges.object: intralysosomal processing into discrete functional peptides
edges.quote: several links between PGRN and the lysosome have been established, including the existence of two independent lysosomal trafficking pathways, intralysosomal processing of PGRN into discrete functional peptides, and direct and indirect regulation of lysosomal hydrolases.
